Position Summary

Mosaic Health is seeking an experienced and relationship-driven Recruiter to join our Talent Acquisition team. Reporting to the Manager, Talent Acquisition, this role will be responsible for managing full-cycle recruiting across a variety of business functions, partnering closely with hiring managers to identify, attract, and hire top talent.

The ideal candidate is proactive, organized, data-driven, and passionate about delivering an exceptional candidate and hiring manager experience. This individual will play a critical role in supporting Mosaic Health's continued growth by developing effective sourcing strategies, managing candidate pipelines, and serving as a trusted talent advisor throughout the hiring process.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Recruiter

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Department: Talent Acquisition
Reports To: Manager, Talent Acquisition
Employment Type: Full-Time

About Mosaic Health

Mosaic Health is dedicated to transforming healthcare through innovative, patient-centered care models that improve outcomes and access. We are building a high-performing team of mission-driven professionals who are passionate about making healthcare better for patients, providers, and communities.

Position Summary

Mosaic Health is seeking an experienced and relationship-driven Recruiter to join our Talent Acquisition team. Reporting to the Manager, Talent Acquisition, this role will be responsible for managing full-cycle recruiting across a variety of business functions, partnering closely with hiring managers to identify, attract, and hire top talent.

The ideal candidate is proactive, organized, data-driven, and passionate about delivering an exceptional candidate and hiring manager experience. This individual will play a critical role in supporting Mosaic Health's continued growth by developing effective sourcing strategies, managing candidate pipelines, and serving as a trusted talent advisor throughout the hiring process.

Key Responsibilities

Full-Cycle Recruitment

  • Manage the end-to-end recruitment process from intake through offer acceptance and onboarding handoff.
  • Partner with hiring managers to understand business needs, role requirements, and ideal candidate profiles.
  • Develop and execute recruiting strategies to attract qualified and diverse talent.
  • Conduct candidate sourcing through job boards, professional networks, referrals, social media, and direct outreach.
  • Screen resumes and conduct initial candidate interviews to assess qualifications, experience, and cultural alignment.
  • Coordinate and facilitate interview processes, ensuring a seamless experience for candidates and interview teams.
  • Manage offer development and negotiation in partnership with hiring managers and Human Resources.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Talent Partnership & Consultation

  • Serve as a strategic advisor to hiring managers on recruiting best practices, market trends, and talent availability.
  • Provide guidance on interview techniques, candidate evaluation, and hiring decisions.
  • Build strong relationships with business leaders and stakeholders across the organization.
  • Ensure consistency and compliance throughout the hiring process.

Candidate Experience

  • Deliver a high-quality, professional, and engaging experience for all candidates.
  • Maintain timely communication with candidates throughout the recruitment lifecycle.
  • Promote Mosaic Health's employer brand and value proposition in all candidate interactions.

Talent Pipeline Development

  • Build and maintain proactive talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs.
  • Leverage market research and sourcing tools to identify top talent.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with passive candidates and industry professionals.

Recruiting Operations & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate candidate records and recruiting activity within the Applicant Tracking System (ATS).
  • Track and report on recruiting metrics, including time-to-fill, pipeline health, and source effectiveness.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives within the Talent Acquisition function.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 3+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, preferably in healthcare, corporate, technology, or high-growth environments.
  • Proven experience sourcing and recruiting for a variety of professional-level roles.
  • Strong interviewing, candidate assessment, and relationship-building skills.
  • Experience using Applicant Tracking Systems and sourcing tools such as LinkedIn Recruiter.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and project management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple requisitions and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering an exceptional candidate experience.

Preferred

  • Experience recruiting within healthcare, value-based care, health technology, or related industries.
  • Experience supporting remote and geographically dispersed teams.
  • Knowledge of employment law and recruiting compliance requirements.
  • Experience utilizing recruiting analytics and workforce planning data to inform hiring strategies.

Competencies

  • Consultative and collaborative approach
  • Strong business acumen
  • Relationship building and stakeholder management
  • Results orientation and accountability
  • Adaptability and problem-solving
  • Attention to detail and operational excellence
  • Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

What You'll Bring

  • A passion for connecting talented individuals with meaningful career opportunities.
  • The ability to influence and build trust with hiring managers and candidates alike.
  • A proactive mindset and continuous improvement mentality.
  • A commitment to supporting Mosaic Health's mission, values, and culture.

Why Join Mosaic Health?

At Mosaic Health, you'll have the opportunity to help build teams that directly impact the future of healthcare. You'll work alongside collaborative colleagues in a mission-driven environment that values innovation, inclusion, and professional growth while enjoying the flexibility of a fully remote work setting.

Mosaic Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants.

Job Title: Associate Director Country Operations Management

Job Location: Munich, Germany

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

This is what you will do:

The Associate Director Country Operations Management (AD COM) reports to the Head of Country Operations. AD COM has the accountability to support the Country strategy implementation, to act as company culture and value ambassador and to act as line manager of local functions as agreed with Head of Country Operations.

The AD COM is accountable for all assigned operational trial deliverables across programs are completed according to timelines, operational procedures, quality standards, SOPs and guidelines, independently if the trial is directly manage by the AD COM or by his/her direct reports.

The Associate Director Country Operations Management (AD COM) is responsible for day-to-day management of a dedicated functional group(s) within Country Operations Management local team, and is responsible for planning and utilization of staff resources, objective setting and performance development. The AD COM is responsible for their direct reports delivery to study expectations.

It is also expected that the AD COM may contribute to regional/global initiatives as delegated.

In some countries AD COM may also take other responsibilities such as Project Manager Country Operations (PMCO) if required, as agreed with the Head of Country Operations (HCO).

You will be responsible for:

  • Leading and developing of the dedicated functional group within Country Operations Management at local level.
  • Ensures adequate resources for the studies assigned, ensure that workload of direct reports is optimized, and ensures appropriate and timely assignment to projects by liaising with relevant stakeholders (HCO, PMCO, global study team, etc).
  • Development and performance management of direct reports, including implementation of development and training plan and regular coaching of the direct reports.
  • Prepares salary and bonus proposals for direct reports based on their performance in close collaboration with responsible HCO
  • Manages new staff interviews, hiring, onboarding process, for full-time and and in-sourced staff
  • Ensures that study activities at country level comply with local policies and code of ethics, and ensures team delivery to committed activation and recruitment targets
  • Contribute to Country feasibility analysis for new potential clinical trials (as applicable, depending on the direct reports the LM will be managing). Support the Country external scientific engagement strategy and action plan.
  • Contribute to efficient COM organization and its functioning at country level by working closely with responsible HCO.
  • Support HCO and in-Country COM activities as agreed with HCO, such as Site Oversight Visit reports review (as applicable, depending on the direct reports the LM will be managing) and onboarding and training of new in-Country COM functions and team members
  • Act as extended local leadership team member with accountability to support the Country strategy implementation, champion the company values and support HCO with the local affiliate and global DRS team cross-functional interactions required to support local COM goals.
  • Contribute to the quality improvement of the study processes and other procedures through close partnership with DCQ at Country level
  • Support inspection readiness activities at site and country level.
  • Collaborates in identifying patient, site or country level quality deficiencies which may lead to the creation quality events/issues, and support in discussions around those as required (i.e: CAPAs). This may include to conduct Site Oversight Visits triggered by observed quality signals

For individuals managing CRAs to:

  • Plan and conduct regular accompanied/assessment visits with CRAs
  • Provides support to their CRAs in managing site issues, from a monitoring perspective, ensuring that monitoring activities are conducted according to expectations.
  • May act as a site liaison with prime sites for Alexion to facilitate discussion and consultation around site compliance to ICH GCP and process improvements, as agreed with their line manager.
  • Collaborates with in-country local roles (PMCO and DCQ) in monitoring quality oversight based on agreed KPIs. Maintain tools to document and track clinical monitoring activities as required.

If AD COM takes other role in combination to current responsibilities, please refer to the corresponding Job description.

You will need to have:

  • Bachelors degree in related discipline, preferably in life science, or equivalent qualification.
  • Minimum 8 ( 5 for LM of CRAs only) years of experience in Development Operations (CRA / Sr. CRA / Project management) or other related fields.
  • Strong leadership to drive team growth, development and support the local COM strategy implementation
  • Pro-active identification of requirements to support future needs
  • Business acumen to understand company direction and drive the understanding at team level
  • Solution oriented attitude and ability to lead through ambiguity
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, proactivity and assertiveness.
  • Manage change with a positive approach for self, team and business. Sees change as an opportunity to improve performance and add value to business.
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, influencing and negotiation skills.
  • Excellent presentation and communication skills, verbal and written.
  • Excellent knowledge of spoken and written English.
  • Ability for national and international travel.
  • Integrity and high ethical standards.

We would prefer for you to have:

  • Line management experience and good resource management skills
  • Prior CRA experience
  • Excellent knowledge of the Monitoring Process.
  • Good understanding of the Study Drug Handling Process and the Data Management Process.
  • Ability to work in an environment of remote collaborators.
  • Excellent decision-making skills.
  • Good conflict management skills and ability to handle crisis.
  • Excellent team building skills also in cross-functional teams.
  • Good intercultural awareness.

jobs.excerpt: Location: Remote (U. S.  or Canada)Type: US Applicants – Full-Time; Canadian Applicants – Independent Contractor About Human AgencyWe're scaling rapidly and have a growing pipeline of opportunities that demand exceptional talent across disciplines.
jobs.description:
Location: Remote (U.S. or Canada)

Type: US Applicants – Full-Time; Canadian Applicants – Independent Contractor

About Human Agency

We're scaling rapidly and have a growing pipeline of opportunities that demand exceptional talent across disciplines. Our mission is to bring on individuals, from creative producers to technical experts to entrepreneurial leaders, who can help us realize this next chapter of growth.

We are a company of doers. Leaders roll up their sleeves, teams work flat, and everyone contributes to what ships. Titles don't insulate us from feedback or basics. We invite critique, learn quickly, and keep raising the bar. The best ideas win here, no matter where they come from, because clients trust us to deliver the strongest outcomes every time.

Our clients' missions, products, and bottom lines are sacred. We immerse ourselves in their world, becoming stewards of their goals and partners in solving big problems. Every product, strategy, or asset we create must be both beautiful and functional; practical, usable, and designed for real-world impact.

Humans are our most valuable resource, and we only grow by hiring people who push us forward. Across strategy, engineering, design, data, and operations, we seek out teammates who raise the bar and make us better. Always hire up, never down.

We partner with organizations of all sizes to explore, design, and implement AI strategies that are secure, scalable, and human-centered. We believe AI should amplify human potential, not replace it, and we build with that conviction in every engagement. From advisory and tooling to implementation and education, we meet clients where they are and help them integrate AI in ways that align with their mission and values. Our goal is to empower teams to work smarter, move faster, and unlock new possibilities through thoughtful, responsible innovation.

And through it all, we lead with purpose, love, and adventure. We do meaningful work with people we care about, and we make the ride an adventure worth taking. Because at Human Agency, who we are and how we work are one and the same.

The Opportunity

This is not a traditional enterprise CISO role where you inherit a legacy infrastructure, manage a large team, and maintain the status quo. This is a hands-on, entrepreneurial builder role. You are joining at the frontier of AI security — designing systems that don't yet exist, solving problems the industry is only beginning to name, and treating security not as a cost center but as a strategic and commercial advantage.

We're deploying AI agents at scale across client environments, building our own AI-powered tools, and advising organizations on how to safely integrate autonomous systems into mission-critical workflows. That creates a unique security mandate: you must secure our internal operations, embed security directly into the AI products we build, and help clients deploy agents safely in regulated, high-stakes environments. You are architect, operator, and evangelist all at once.

You'll have the rare opportunity to shape how an entire category of technology gets secured. We're not asking you to retrofit old playbooks onto new problems — we're asking you to write the playbook. If you've been looking for a role where security is core to the product, where you can build things that matter, and where your work influences the broader conversation around AI safety and governance, this is it.

What You'll Own

Define and execute our security strategy from the ground up. You'll architect our internal security posture across infrastructure, data, and AI systems, establish governance models for how we deploy agents safely, and ensure we're prepared for compliance frameworks like SOC 2, ISO, and potentially FedRAMP as we scale into enterprise and government clients.

Build security into AI agent systems as a first-class product feature. You'll design guardrails, monitoring, and policy enforcement for autonomous agents — ensuring they operate within defined boundaries, audit their own actions, and surface anomalies in real time. This isn't theoretical; you'll implement these systems in production environments where they directly impact client outcomes.

Develop and potentially commercialize security products. The security tooling you build internally may become standalone offerings. You'll have the latitude to identify what's missing in the market, prototype solutions, and work with our product and engineering teams to turn internal infrastructure into revenue-generating products.

Lead incident response, threat modeling, and adversarial testing. You'll build and run red team exercises against our AI systems, model attack vectors that don't yet have names, and develop response frameworks for risks unique to agentic AI — things like prompt injection at scale, model extraction, or adversarial manipulation of agent behavior.

Serve as the public face of AI security for Human Agency. You'll represent us in client conversations, partner discussions, and industry forums. You'll publish, speak, and help shape the broader conversation around AI risk, alignment, and governance. If the industry doesn't yet have consensus on how to secure a given AI capability, you'll be one of the people defining it.

Deploy and operate security infrastructure hands-on. You'll implement zero-trust architectures, secure multi-agent systems, deploy monitoring and detection tools, and build secure data pipelines. This is not a role where you delegate all technical work — you write code, you configure systems, you debug in production when necessary.

Who You Are

Experience & Skills

  • You've served as a CISO, VP of Security, or Head of Security at a high-growth tech company, ideally one building or deploying AI systems at scale.
  • You have deep, hands-on experience securing AI and machine learning systems — not just theoretical knowledge, but real work protecting LLM architectures, model training pipelines, and inference infrastructure.
  • You've built and operated cloud-native security programs across AWS, GCP, or Azure, including zero-trust frameworks, identity and access management, and secure multi-tenant architectures.
  • You understand threat modeling and red teaming deeply, and you've led adversarial exercises against complex systems — ideally including AI-specific attack vectors like prompt injection, model inversion, or data poisoning.
  • You've designed and implemented security monitoring, incident response, and compliance programs that scale — you know what good looks like at every stage from startup to enterprise readiness.
  • You have a track record of building or contributing to security products, not just internal programs — something you shipped that customers used, or tooling that became infrastructure for others.

Mindset & Traits

  • You think like a founder. You see security as a competitive advantage and a product opportunity, not just a compliance checkbox. You want to build things, not just manage them.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and energized by unsolved problems. The fact that no one has secured autonomous AI agents at scale yet doesn't intimidate you — it excites you.
  • You are product-minded and commercially aware. You understand that security decisions have business implications, and you can articulate trade-offs in language that non-security stakeholders understand and respect.
  • You are technical enough to earn respect from engineers and pragmatic enough to earn trust from clients. You can debug a containerized agent deployment in the morning and present to a CFO in the afternoon.
  • You are a teacher and a builder of institutional knowledge. You document what you learn, you share what you know, and you leave systems better than you found them.
  • You care deeply about doing the right thing. You take security seriously because real people and real organizations depend on it, and you hold yourself to the highest standard even when no one is watching.

Equal Opportunity Commitment

Human Agency is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building inclusive, high-performing teams where everyone can do their best work.

As a Senior System Designer, you will report to the Lead designer and you will work directly with the team members, designers, artists, data scientists and developers.

About NOCD:

Despite being ranked by the World Health Organization as a top 10 most disabling condition, having a lifetime prevalence of over 2%, and causing people to be 10 times more likely to die by suicide, OCD is commonly misrepresented as a personality quirk. Moreover, the "gold-standard" treatment for OCD called Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) has never been widely-accessible. The mission of NOCD is to ensure everyone with OCD knows they are not alone and has access to evidenced based care. Our company started after our founders' own experience with OCD - trying to understand what was happening, going through various misdiagnoses, and finally working with an ERP specialist to get better. We recently raised a series A round and need the help of those who are passionate about our mission to serve those with OCD.

What we're looking for:

  • Passion for our mission and empathy for our members- building for members means learning about what they're going through. We'll send you resources about OCD is from a members perspective and how it's managed from a clinical perspective

  • High Agency and bias to action- We are still a small company and there's a lot of work to do. We trust everyone we hire and will provide them any support they need

  • Abundance and growth mindset- There is always more we can do to serve our members. We hope this will be one of the most rewarding professional experiences of your career.

  • Clear communication- Ideas are better when shared so we hope that you can share them with others in written form.

  • 5 + years of experience- You care about what you're building and have built significant production systems in the past. You are comfortable moving across the stack when necessary

  • Building an amazing user experience with our iOS app

Tools we use:

  • Web : NextJS / Typescript / Tailwind CSS / Netlify / React

Position Title:

Job Description:

The Center for Industrial Research and Service (CIRAS) is seeking a Growth Services Manager to help companies throughout Iowa identify growth opportunities, solve marketing and sales challenges, and strengthen, expand, and retain revenue. In this role, you will work directly with leaders of small- to mid-sized businesses to understand their markets and business objectives, diagnose root-cause issues, and guide them toward practical strategies and solutions that improve business performance.

This position blends marketing and growth expertise with hands-on consulting, business development, project leadership, and relationship building. You will lead client engagements involving marketing strategy, digital marketing, customer discovery, competitive analysis, market research, sales process improvement, positioning and value proposition development, and new product or market opportunities. You will not necessarily be the deepest technical expert in every area. Rather, you must have sufficient marketing and digital marketing knowledge to diagnose client needs, develop sound strategies, ask informed questions, evaluate potential solutions, and determine when specialized expertise is needed. Working with clients, CIRAS colleagues, and third-party specialists, you will integrate that expertise into practical solutions that address the client's underlying business needs.

The ideal candidate brings a passion for helping people and businesses succeed, along with experience applying marketing, sales, and business development practices to achieve measurable results. Success requires a strong foundation in marketing strategy and working knowledge of digital marketing sufficient to diagnose needs, ask informed questions, evaluate recommendations, and work effectively with specialists. Just as important are initiative, sound business judgment, curiosity, organization, follow-through, and the ability to influence others without relying on formal authority. The successful candidate will be comfortable acknowledging the limits of their expertise and actively seeking additional knowledge or specialized resources when client needs require it.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop client opportunities through professional relationships, educational activities, networking, referrals, existing clients, and collaboration with CIRAS colleagues.
  • Apply knowledge of marketing, sales, digital marketing, and other growth-related practices to help clients identify appropriate strategies and solutions that achieve business results.
  • Engage clients in a consultative manner to clarify root-cause issues, determine what they need rather than simply what they request, propose appropriate solutions, and create alignment and support for action.
  • Translate client needs into clear, actionable project scopes, including proposal development, budgeting, expected outcomes, value communication, and alignment on execution expectations.
  • Identify when specialized expertise is needed; select and engage appropriate CIRAS or third-party resources; and provide sufficient leadership and subject-matter judgment to evaluate, challenge when appropriate, and integrate specialized recommendations into coherent client solutions.
  • Present recommendations and proposals, communicate business value, address concerns and objections, and guide clients toward informed decisions and commitment.
  • Lead and manage complex client engagements from opportunity through implementation, often involving clients, third-party resources, CIRAS colleagues, and multiple business disciplines; anticipate and resolve issues, maintain stakeholder accountability, and keep delivery aligned with approved strategy, scope, timeline, budget, and expected outcomes.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, third-party resources, colleagues, and other stakeholders; identify evolving needs and additional opportunities where CIRAS can create value.
  • Plan and facilitate workshops, webinars, training sessions, and client discussions that build capability, strengthen relationships, and create business opportunities.
  • Manage project scope, timelines, budgets, deliverables, communications, documentation, invoicing, and other administrative requirements; evaluate completed engagements and ensure appropriate project closeout.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business management, or a related field.
  • 5-10 years of progressive experience in marketing, business development, consulting, or related work, including demonstrated responsibility for leading initiatives involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated understanding of marketing strategy, including segmentation and targeting, positioning and value propositions, customer and market research, marketing planning, lead generation, digital marketing, and the relationship between marketing and sales.
  • Experience working directly with business leaders to diagnose needs, distinguish underlying business problems from requested solutions, develop recommendations, and translate strategy into action.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead projects and initiatives through others, including organizing work, engaging internal or external subject-matter experts, resolving issues, maintaining accountability, and driving work to completion.
  • Experience developing business opportunities through relationships, networking, referrals, educational activities, or consultative selling.
  • Experience working with small- to mid-sized businesses and/or manufacturers is preferred.

About the Department:

The Center for Industrial Research and Service (CIRAS) helps Iowa businesses solve complex problems and move forward with confidence.

As part of the Iowa State University College of Engineering and Economic Development and Industry Relations, we connect companies to innovative expertise, applied research, and strategic resources that drive real results.

Since 1963, CIRAS has partnered with Iowa businesses to strengthen leadership, improve operations, grow markets, and build skilled workforces. We bring practical industry knowledge, an objective perspective, and access to a powerful statewide network.

For more information visit the CIRAS Website

What you will bring

A desire to drive your future and accelerate your career. You will bring experience and knowledge in:

  • Leading quality assurance and testing workstreams for large-scale ERP, supply chain, or enterprise platform transformation programs in the CPG or FMCG industry.
  • Hands-on expertise with test automation tools, specifically Selenium (for web-based UI automation) and TOSCA (Tricentis) for end-to-end test automation and continuous testing.
  • Test management tools such as JIRA/Zephyr, ALM (HP Quality Center), Azure DevOps, or equivalent platforms for managing test cases, cycles, and defect tracking.
  • Designing and executing SIT, UAT, regression, and performance testing strategies for complex, multi-system landscapes including ERP (SAP), planning platforms (o9, IBP), and integrated non-SAP applications.
  • Stakeholder management — communicating testing status, risks, and quality outcomes clearly to both technical teams and senior business leadership across multiple regions and functions.
  • Driving UAT processes including test scenario design with business users, defect triage sessions, exit criteria definition, and formal sign-off procedures.
  • Agile and waterfall delivery methodologies, with the ability to adapt testing approaches to program context.
  • Working in global, matrixed organizations with geographically distributed teams and multiple vendor partners.
  • Risk-based testing approaches — identifying critical test scenarios and prioritizing coverage based on business impact.
  • Building and maintaining reusable test asset libraries that accelerate future testing cycles and regression runs.

More about this role

What you need to know about this position:

  • This role is a key leadership position within the o9 EOP program and will support UAT, SIT, and Go-Live testing activities across all wave deployments.
  • The Testing Lead will coordinate closely with the Solution Architect, Integration teams, Business Process Owners, and the o9 vendor team to ensure full end-to-end test coverage.
  • The role requires strong organizational skills to manage parallel testing workstreams across multiple regions and business functions simultaneously.
  • This position sits within the Digital & Technology function and reports into the o9 Program Leadership / Quality Assurance Lead.

What extra ingredients you will bring:

  • Experience testing o9 Solutions, SAP IBP, SAP S/4HANA, or equivalent enterprise supply chain and planning platforms.
  • Familiarity with supply chain planning processes — Demand Planning, Supply Planning, S&OP, Trade Promotion Management (TPM) — and the ability to translate business scenarios into effective test cases.
  • Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps practices, with experience integrating automated tests into build and release pipelines.
  • Exposure to AI-powered testing tools or intelligent test automation practices is a plus.
  • Experience with data validation testing — including master data, transactional data, and integration payload verification across system boundaries.

Education / Certifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. An engineering background is strongly preferred.
  • ISTQB certification (Foundation, Advanced Test Manager, or Agile Tester) is highly desirable.
  • Tricentis TOSCA certification (e.g., TOSCA Automation Specialist Level 1 or 2) is a strong advantage.
  • SAP or o9 functional knowledge certifications are a plus.
  • Project Management certifications (PMP, PRINCE2, or SAFe) are beneficial given the stakeholder and program management scope of this role.

Job specific requirements:

  • Minimum 8–10 years of experience in QA and software testing roles, with at least 4–5 years in a test lead or test manager capacity on large transformation programs.
  • Proven track record of successfully leading UAT exit approvals and Go-Live readiness validations for enterprise platform programs.
  • Demonstrated experience managing and reporting to senior stakeholders across business and IT in a global CPG or FMCG environment.
  • Strong hands-on experience with both Selenium and TOSCA automation frameworks is mandatory.

Travel requirements:

  • Occasional travel may be required to support regional testing activities and stakeholder workshops across NALA, MEU, and AMEA.

Work schedule:

  • Full-time. Flexible working arrangements available in line with MDLZ policy. Ability to accommodate cross-regional time zones is required during peak testing cycles and UAT phases.
No Relocation support available

Headquartered in Singapore, Mondelēz International’s Asia, Middle East and Africa (AMEA) region is comprised of six business units, has more than 21,000 employees and operates in more than 27 countries including Australia, China, Indonesia, Ghana, India, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Philippines, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Thailand, United Arab Emirates and Vietnam. Seventy-six nationalities work across a network of more than 35 manufacturing plants, three global research and development technical centers and in offices stretching from Auckland, New Zealand to Casablanca, Morocco.   • Bachelor’s degree (or above) with at least 4 years of direct site management (monitoring) experience in a bio / pharma / CRO.

If you’re passionate about helping people protect what matters most to them at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, as well as innovating and simplifying processes and operations to provide the best customer value, then Nationwide’s Property and Casualty team could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

Location: Preferred location is Columbus, OH; however, this role is available to remote candidates as well. Remote or hybrid candidates with the desired experience will be considered.

This role will serve as referral underwriting leaderfor complex Global Property and Casualty,Middle Market multinational accountssourced by N2G, a joint venture created by two insurance powerhouses: Nationwide Mutual Insurance Company (Nationwide®) and Generali Global Corporate & Commercial.

In this role, you will serve as thetechnicalunderwritingauthority responsible for evaluating complex and high-exposure property and casualty risks within the Middle Market segment. This role serves as a key referral point for underwriting teams,providingexpert guidance, ensuring adherence to underwriting standards, and supporting profitable growth across global portfolios.

The position partners closely with underwriting, actuarial, product, and riskengineeringteams to drive disciplined underwriting practices, enhance technical capabilities, andmaintainconsistency in risk selection and pricing.

Job Description Summary

Are you a proven Industry leader with strategic, creative and technical commercial product and underwriting skills? Do you have deep insights in specific commercial industry segments as well as industry competitors? Can you translate those insights into strategic and technical underwriting practices and partner with teams to implement the best practices? If you have these abilities, set strategic vision and a drive to achieve financial goals, then we want to hear from you!

As a Technical Director, you will be the leader assigned to a specific industry, responsible for developing and recommending profit strategies with execution of underwriting standards. The Technical Director will be the subject matter expert as it pertains to the review of referrals, pricing strategy, growth and profitability of assigned industries. You will collaborate with Loss Control, Claims, Underwriting and practice leaders to ensure alignment to the strategic direction your assigned industries. You are responsible for underwriting execution where specialization is critical, and to create profit, and growth strategies for the assigned industry in conjunction with field leaders. The role requires a strong technical ability for the assigned industry business, as well as an understanding of the brokerage and property and casualty landscape.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for assisting in the development and implementation of strategic long and short-range plans to drive profitable business opportunities within assigned Commercial Middle Market industry segment(s). Monitors industry portfolio management to verify risk selection and quality are in alignment with risk appetite and strategy.

  • Responsible for providing guidance, direction and authority on industry practice referrals. Maintains appropriate level of authority in providing technical assistance and support to underwriting teams across the country. Serves as technical expert to provide technical advice for assigned industry segments to provide technical underwriting consultation using office hours, new business roundtables and team huddles while fostering a collaborative environment.

  • Within assigned industry segment(s), advises the national field underwriting organization through effective risk selection, agent/broker relationships, portfolio management, mix of business, CAT exposure management, quality underwriting decisions and territory performance in line with business strategy.

  • Collaborates with industry business leaders and field underwriting teams to establish and maintain underwriting guidelines, authority, appetite, underwriting standards while developing strategies for retention and new business.

  • Regularly collaborates with Risk Management and Claims teams to learn about trends and insights while making recommendations in underwriting practice, capabilities or service offerings. Monitors loss trends, regulatory changes, and emerging hazards for assigned industry segment(s) and assists in the implementation of continuous improvement strategies for stronger portfolio performance.

  • Regularly collaborates with product/portfolio, line of business experts, underwriting capabilities, and inside/field underwriting leadership teams as it relates to executing on the assigned industry strategy. Collaborates with actuary to understand and refine pricing models aligned with assigned industry. Supports reinsurance placement and policy limits management.

  • Fosters a continuous learning and development culture. Educates the field underwriting teams through industry segment(s) specific knowledge, including insurance principles, industry trends and risk factors. Provides mentoring and coaching to the field underwriting teams. Assists in the development and co-facilitation of training, capabilities, or enterprise-wide initiatives.

  • Participates in broker visits and industry events to strengthen relationships and gain market insights. Interacts with key brokers, agents, and clients to build strong relationships as part of the stewardship process. Assists in the creation of industry white papers to advance technical competency.

  • Completes underwriting quality reviews to confirm alignment with underwriting strategy and expectations for assigned industry segment(s).

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: AVP, Industry Segment, Middle Market

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate studies preferably in business or a related field, graduate studies preferred.

License/Certification/Designation: CPCU, ARM or other industry designations preferred.

Experience: Typically, 10+ years of Middle Market and/or other related commercial lines underwriting experience to include extensive technical understanding of assigned industry segment(s).

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Comprehensive industry knowledge including underwriting, pricing, operations, producer management, competitive landscape and product development. Demonstrated ability to drive for results. Strong industry underwriting acumen. Strong competency in strategic and organizational agility while fostering a collaborative underwriting environment. Proven communication, collaboration, relationship management, influencing skills, customer focus and conflict resolution skills. Advanced level of industry underwriting expertise. Knowledge of commercial property & casualty products, finance and actuarial concepts; regulatory environment; reinsurance; account management. Strategic analyzing and problem solving of risks; decision making, courage; and innovation. Ability to communicate effectively while engaging and motivating people; negotiation; influencing others; focusing on service; managing and improving processes; executing, planning and organizing work.

Other criteria, including leadership skills, competencies and experiences may take precedence.

The Communications Liaison will provide writing, editing, and communications support for the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) patient safety and compliance program. This role is responsible for technical editing of all contract deliverables, reviewing and refining materials for OPTN committee and Board meetings, coordinating public-facing communications, and serving as the primary liaison between the project team and HRSA/OPTN communications staff.

The Communications Specialist ensures that written products are clear, accurate, consistent with federal plain language and branding requirements, and compliant with HRSA/OPTN review processes. This role combines strong editorial skills, stakeholder coordination, and knowledge of federal communication standards to support transparent, high-quality communication about OPTN patient safety, membership, and compliance activities.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Editing and Quality Control of Deliverables

  • Perform detailed technical editing, copyediting, and proofreading of all written deliverables under the contract (e.g., plans, SOPs, reports, meeting summaries, training materials).

  • Ensure consistency in style, tone, terminology, and formatting across documents and presentations.

  • Apply federal Plain Language Guidelines and HRSA/OPTN style and branding requirements to all materials.

  • Review documents for clarity, logical flow, and alignment with program objectives and regulatory context; work with technical leads to resolve ambiguities and strengthen key messages.

  • Support the development and maintenance of editorial standards, templates, and checklists for project deliverables.

2. Committee and Board Materials Support

  • Review and refine slide decks, briefing documents, talking points, and other materials prepared for Safety and Compliance Committee(s), OPTN Board, and related workgroups.

  • Ensure meeting materials clearly describe goals, decisions needed, and key background information, and are appropriate for the intended audience (e.g., clinical, technical, leadership, public).

  • Check all materials for accuracy, completeness, and adherence to confidentiality, redaction, and sensitive information requirements.

  • Coordinate timelines for materials review and finalization to meet established deadlines for committee and Board meetings.

3. Public-Facing Communications

  • Draft, edit, and format public-facing content describing Safety and Compliance Committee(s) activities, membership, accomplishments, and key policy or program updates (e.g., website content, fact sheets, summaries).

  • Ensure all public materials:

    • Follow OPTN branding and HRSA communications guidance.

    • Use plain language and are accessible to non-technical audiences.

    • Comply with federal requirements (e.g., no lobbying, no commercial advertising, no non-federal logos outside OPTN).

  • Support preparation of de-identified, public-facing meeting summaries and other materials for posting to the OPTN website.

  • Assist in developing standard templates and messaging for recurring public communications.

4. Liaison to HRSA/OPTN Communications

  • Serve as the primary day-to-day point of contact between the project team and HRSA/OPTN communications staff.

  • Coordinate routing of draft public materials for review and written approval from the COR and HRSA/OPTN communications team, per contract requirements.

  • Track communications requests from HRSA and ensure timely, complete responses in coordination with internal subject matter experts.

  • Maintain documentation of approvals, branding guidance, and communications SOPs, and ensure the project team applies them consistently.

5. Internal Coordination and Support

  • Work closely with project managers, committee operations staff, analysts, and subject matter experts to understand content, context, and intended audiences for deliverables.

  • Support preparation of visually clear, accessible materials (e.g., charts, tables, graphics) in alignment with Section 508 accessibility requirements.

  • Contribute to continuous improvement of communication products and processes, including recommending updates to templates, workflows, and review processes.

  • Help ensure that all communications-related tasks and timelines are integrated into project plans and tracking tools.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, English, Public Health, Public Policy, Health Administration, Journalism, or a related field.

  • Master’s degree in a related field is preferred but not required.

Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in technical editing, communications, or similar roles supporting complex programs or projects.

  • Experience working with or supporting federal agencies, healthcare, public health, or regulatory/compliance environments is strongly preferred.

  • Prior experience supporting leadership, committee, or board-level communications is a plus.

Skills and Competencies

  • Technical Editing & Writing: Demonstrated ability to edit complex, technical content for clarity, consistency, and readability while preserving accuracy.

  • Plain Language & Policy Translation: Skilled at translating technical and regulatory concepts into clear, accessible language for diverse audiences.

  • Attention to Detail: Exceptional accuracy in grammar, formatting, and content review; strong ability to identify inconsistencies and gaps.

  • Compliance & Branding Awareness: Familiarity with, or ability to quickly learn, federal plain language requirements, branding guidelines, and restrictions on lobbying and advertising.

  • Stakeholder Coordination: Experience working with multiple stakeholders (e.g., program staff, clinicians, policy experts, communications offices) to refine and finalize materials.

  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide constructive editorial feedback and to clarify complex content with subject matter experts.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), SharePoint/Teams, and virtual meeting platforms; experience preparing accessible documents (Section 508) is preferred.

  • Organization & Time Management: Ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines, prioritize work in a fast-paced environment, and meet quality and timeliness expectations.

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT:

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for:

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard:
Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

Requirements and benefits

Educational qualifications

  • A Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science / Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics / Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Systems or other related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree is accepted if only candidate has 5 years of experience in the field.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a minimum of 3 years of professional experience in related roles or domain - specifically for QA-automation/testing or cybersecurity roles

How it works
Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Compensation:
Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $40/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Why this freelance opportunity might be a great fit for you?

  • Take part in a part-time, remote, freelance project that fits around your primary professional or academic commitments.
  • Work on advanced AI projects and gain valuable experience that enhances your portfolio. - Influence how future AI models understand and communicate in your field of expertise.

Open source software is the new default in the enterprise, and Canonical is the new challenger to major enterprise software vendors.

We are profitable and growing our global enterprise sales organisation. We are hiring a regional sales renewal team manager in North America to lead the renewals team in the region.

We deliver better open source from the data center to cloud and edge. Our Linux distribution Ubuntu is now the leading platform for public cloud compute, and the favorite platform for software engineers, data scientists and AI developers. Our mission is to accelerate the adoption and quality of open source globally, and our goal is to ship the most software on the planet by cores. A tidal wave of open source innovation is the next phase of the entire enterprise software industry, and we aim to be the most compelling way to ride that wave.

Our customers include Global 500 enterprises and startups. We are expanding our product range from the base operating system - Ubuntu - to full enterprise solutions in infrastructure and applications. We can deliver software defined storage, private cloud solutions, container runtime environments, as well as databases, message queues, identity, observability, analytics, machine learning and web publishing capabilities. Customers love the idea that they can get security compliance and support for everything open source from a single company. Our goal is to have more solutions on tap than any other vendor, and we have built unique capabilities to make that possible across every cloud, every class of compute and every category of application.

Canonical provides licensed enterprise software products, commercial support, managed services, consulting and training services to customers who are deploying Ubuntu or open source applications on the cloud, in their data center, or to the connected device and IoT ecosystem. We are just over 1,000 colleagues in 70+ countries and over $250m in revenue, profitable, on a steady but relentless growth trajectory. We are almost entirely distributed, with leadership spread across many countries. We believe that talent is equally distributed across the globe, and we are excited to hire, develop, promote and ultimately trust a diverse group of exceptional leads to build the best, not biggest, enterprise software company.

We hire carefully and deliberately; our selection process is long and requires substantial work from applicants. It will take successful applicants three to six months to secure an offer. This is not a place to apply if you are in a rush to find a position, it is a worthwhile place to apply if you are ambitious and long-term in your thinking about your career and the dynamics which move the world forward. If you see clearly the rise of open source, and you understand the drivers of enterprise procurement and technical decision making, then you will understand why Canonical has such a tremendous long term advantage. You will also understand, given the ferocity of competition and the challenges of competing in a market of giants, that we have to set a very high bar for hiring and performance. In order to be a world leading company we select for exceptional ability as well as character, and then provide an environment which promotes teamwork and celebrates diligence, collaboration and effectiveness. All of those are easy to say but hard to do - at Canonical we are willing to be uncomfortable in pursuit of that excellence.

In building our sales team, we look for five things:

  • Empathy for the customer - a real understanding of customer needs, industry-specific challenges, and a desire to help customers solve their business problems
  • High intellect - the ability to learn quickly, understand very complex subjects, and communicate clearly to build trust and confidence
  • Passion for technology - a fascination with the state of the art from brilliant people solving hard problems, and fierce competition for large prizes
  • Teamwork - a willingness to help others, to collaborate well with people from different disciplines, and to balance personal and team ambitions
  • Energy - the drive to motivate oneself and others to achieve the best result for the team and our customers

Ubuntu is already very widely adopted which gives us a credible basis for conversations in the market. Nevertheless, it requires real work for sales professionals to build on that adoption to create trusted and profitable commercial relationships with the enterprises in their territory. Our product managers and marketing teams run campaigns to generate awareness, engagement and leads, but you will need to go beyond managing inbound interest to develop the potential of your territory. You will need judgement as to which industries and companies are ready to go deeper with open source and Canonical, and energy to develop relationships in advance of proven interest. We expect professional practice, territory and account planning, as well as clear, complete and continuous reporting on pipeline status and activity, using standard professional tools.

The successful candidate will carry an annual team bookings quota within their territory. They should be able to travel regionally for client engagements or, industry conferences, and internationally for company events twice a year. They will be expected to demonstrate professionalism and effectiveness in managing their team. They will need to coach, mentor and lead by example. Their sales representatives are expected to prospect accounts for new business, maintain and develop existing relationships, and work with colleagues and partners on account strategy. They must be comfortable selling enterprise software, open source, cloud, virtualization, container technologies and technical software solutions to senior levels of the enterprise.

jobs.excerpt: Geode Health is a rapidly growing, national provider of outpatient mental health services.
jobs.description:
Geode Health is a rapidly growing, national provider of outpatient mental health services. Our Mission is to “Transform mental health by making it more accessible, affordable and effective”.

Position Type: Full-Time |Remote |Hourly, Non-Exempt

Compensation: $20 / hour

Schedule: Full-time shifts within center hours of operation, Monday–Sunday (Central/Eastern coverage); some evenings and weekends

Who We Are

Geode Health is a rapidly growing, national provider of outpatient mental health services. Our mission is to empower our patients to live healthier, more rewarding lives through accessible, affordable, and effective mental healthcare tailored to their needs. Our Patient Support Center is the front door to that care, often a patient’s first human connection with Geode and the first step in removing barriers between someone seeking help and the provider who can support them.

The Role

The Patient Support Specialist is a high-impact, phone-first role at the heart of patient access and acquisition. You are an ambassador for patients and care teams and the first voice many prospective patients hear and a key partner in helping them move from interest or referral to a scheduled first visit. You’ll turn high-intent inbound calls, referral callbacks, and web leads into appointments while delivering a warm, hospitality-driven experience. A smaller share of your day is spent helping established patients by resolving simple requests or routing them to the right team.

This is a fast-paced, quality-focused environment for people who care deeply about both outcomes and experience. You’ll use strong virtual human connection, sound judgment, and customer-centric problem solving to remove barriers to care, connect each patient to the right provider, and help activate a trusted relationship with their care team. If you bring empathy, urgency, and a growth mindset, and believe every call is an opportunity to help someone take the next step, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do

Convert High-Intent Inbound Calls

  • Answer new patient inbound calls, including referral callbacks and consumerleads with warmth, urgency, and a bias toward booking the first visit.
  • Match each patient to the right provider using screening questions, insurance, provider preferences, and scheduling tools to secure the best-fit appointment.
  • Guide ambivalent or hesitant callers toward a confident “yes” using empathy, reflective listening, communication frameworksand sound judgment while removing barriers without pressure.
  • Set clear expectations for the first visit so patients arrive informed, comfortable, and ready to attend.
  • Collaborate with internal teams when needed to resolve open questions and create a seamless handoff for patients and providers.

Support Established Patients

  • Handle a smaller volume of established-patient contacts, resolving simple requests or routing to the right team quickly and accurately.
  • Capture complete, accurate patient context and insurance information; follow up to close any gaps.

Grow Through Coaching & Quality

  • Work toward individual and team goals for conversion, answer rate/service level, quality, and after-call work, using feedback and performance insights to keep improving.
  • Welcome regular call auditing and coaching as fuel for growth; apply feedback quickly and consistently.
  • Document every interaction accurately in our systems with the right context and a clear next step for each patient.

Own Patient Experience

  • Create a calm, personalized experience that helps patients feel confident taking the next step in care.
  • Protect patient privacy by maintaining strict confidentiality and following HIPAA and all privacy requirements.
  • Flex with changing workflows, volumes, and schedules while supporting the broader team as needs shift.

Who You Are

  • A hospitality-minded people person - you make others feel genuinely cared for and you love creating great experiences.
  • Motivated by goals and comfortable using feedback and performance insights to improve.
  • A persuasive, empathetic communicator who can navigate emotional or complex conversations with calm and confidence.
  • You stay organized and calm while handling multiple systems, changing priorities, and a high volume of calls.
  • Coachable and self-aware - you welcome feedback, know your strengths, and actively develop your areas of opportunity.
  • Passionate about mental healthcare and Geode’s mission to expand access to exceptional care.

What You Bring

  • 1–3+ years in a customer-facing, phone-based, or hospitality role; healthcare, call center, or sales/conversion experience is a strong plus.
  • Comfort working in a goal-oriented, quality-focused environment.
  • Familiarity with insurance plans and benefits, or the ability to learn them quickly (preferred).
  • Strong computer skills and the ability to navigate multiple systems while maintaining a warm, focused conversation with the patient.
  • A quiet, professional remote workspace and reliable connectivity.
  • Associate’s or bachelor’s degree preferred.

At Geode Health, we offer:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Flexible schedule

  • In-person and virtual patient visits

  • Comprehensive admin support (front office, accounting, finance, payroll, HR, etc)

  • Professional development opportunities

  • Clinical community, support, and leadership

  • Medical, dental and vision benefits

  • Life insurance

  • Short and long-term disability

  • Paid vacation and holidays

  • Matching 401k plan

  • State of the art technology

Why work for Geode Health?

At Geode Health, we take our commitment to patients and providers seriously. We focus every day on how to help patients across the United States get the best possible mental health care available. To achieve this, we focus on ensuring our providers have unmatched support and resources so that they can focus on providing great care. We are backed by KKR, a leading private equity firm with the experience and mission alignment to truly make an impact. Joining Geode Health will put you on the front-end of a rapidly growing movement to increase access and improve outcomes for mental health patients and providers across the nation.

To learn more, visit us as

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

‎

Commercial Organization | GTM Enablement

Reports to: Director, GTM Enablement

The Lead, Channel Enablement owns the enablement strategy and infrastructure that helps Castlight-powered solutions get sold effectively through our channel ecosystem, including health plans, strategic partners, resellers, and Marketplace relationships.

This role is the Commercial owner of the second sale enablement motion and the connective tissue across Castlight, our partners, and the teams responsible for bringing our solutions to market. The Lead builds the training, demos, tools, and repeatable programs that allow partner sellers and Castlight teams to confidently position, demonstrate, and sell Castlight-powered solutions at scale.

The role also owns the core demo infrastructure supporting channel selling, ensuring our Figma environments, screen libraries, and partner-specific experiences stay current as the product evolves.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

What You'll Own

Channel & Partner Enablement

  • Build and own the channel enablement strategy across health plans, strategic partners, resellers, and Marketplace partners.

  • Develop scalable enablement programs that help partner sellers understand the buyer problem, articulate the Castlight value proposition, demonstrate the solution, and advance opportunities.

  • Create partner-ready training programs, playbooks, talk tracks, FAQs, objection handling, templates, and selling tools using Product Marketing's approved positioning and messaging.

  • Partner with Strategic Partnerships to build tailored enablement programs based on partner type, commercial model, seller audience, and go-to-market motion.

  • Support the launch and ongoing readiness of new partner relationships and Castlight-powered offerings.

Second Sale Enablement

  • Own the enablement framework for the second sale motion across health plan and partner channels.

  • Establish one source of truth for second sale training, demos, tools, templates, and selling standards.

  • Prepare Castlight Commercial and Client teams for the transition of second sale execution to Client CSMs by September 30.

  • Build repeatable training and certification approaches that allow Client teams to execute consistently while maintaining Commercial standards.

  • Create scalable processes for Commercial review, feedback, and continuous improvement as execution moves closer to the client and health plan teams.

Demo Strategy & Engineering

  • Own the core demo environments supporting health plan, partner, reseller, and second sale motions.

  • Build and maintain Figma-based demos, screen libraries, reusable components, and partner-specific demo experiences.

  • Maintain demo environments as products, capabilities, positioning, and user experiences evolve.

  • Lead Nova conversions across the existing channel book and establish the standards for new partner implementations.

  • Manage partner access to demo environments and establish clear governance around version control, usage, and updates.

  • Coordinate external design or Figma resources as needed to maintain and scale the demo platform.

  • Establish a regular operating cadence with Product, UX, Solutions, and Product Marketing so demo experiences remain accurate and current.

Cross-Functional Enablement

  • Translate Product Marketing's positioning and messaging into usable seller training, demos, and field tools.

  • Partner with Strategic Partnerships to understand partner priorities, seller needs, and commercial opportunities.

  • Partner with Client leadership to ensure second sale teams have the tools, training, and confidence required to execute.

  • Partner with Solutions and Product teams to keep demonstrations accurate and identify opportunities to improve how Castlight capabilities are represented in market.

  • Bring health plan, partner, seller, and field feedback back to Product Marketing, Product, Solutions, and Strategic Partnerships to improve messaging, products, and the partner experience.

How Ownership Works

This role operates across several teams, with clear ownership boundaries:

Product Marketing owns core positioning, messaging architecture, value propositions, competitive strategy, and master marketing assets.

Channel Enablement turns that strategy into training, demos, playbooks, tools, certification, and scalable seller experiences.

Strategic Partnerships owns partner strategy, relationships, commercial agreements, partner performance, and escalations.

Client CSMs own plan-specific second sale execution, including training delivery to health plan sellers and ongoing maintenance of client-specific materials.

Solutions and Product provide product expertise, roadmap input, and validation required to keep demonstrations technically accurate.

What Success Looks Like

  • Partner sellers can confidently explain and demonstrate Castlight-powered solutions without relying on Castlight for every selling interaction.

  • Health plan and partner channels have consistent, current, easy-to-use enablement resources.

  • Second sale execution successfully transitions to Client teams without losing quality or commercial consistency.

  • Demo environments stay aligned with the live product and can be efficiently adapted across partners and channels.

  • New partners can move from agreement to seller readiness through a repeatable enablement process.

  • Feedback from partner and second sale motions consistently reaches the teams responsible for product, messaging, and commercial strategy.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in sales enablement, partner enablement, solutions consulting, product marketing support, or a related commercial role, ideally within healthcare technology, employee benefits, or health plans.

  • Experience building enablement programs for channel, partner, reseller, or indirect sales teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex products and positioning into practical tools that sellers can use.

  • Experience building and maintaining demo environments at scale.

  • Strong Figma skills with the ability to manage production-quality demo environments, reusable components, and screen libraries.

  • Strong training and facilitation skills across both internal and external seller audiences.

  • Excellent project management skills with the ability to coordinate Product, UX, Product Marketing, Client, Commercial, and external agency partners.

  • Working knowledge of health plan go-to-market models, white-labeled solutions, or embedded technology partnerships.

  • Comfortable operating in an environment where ownership crosses organizational boundaries and success depends on influence, structure, and follow-through.

What Makes Someone Great in This Role

You are equal parts builder, trainer, and operator. You can take a product strategy or message and turn it into something a seller can actually use. You care about the details of a demo experience, but you also understand the commercial outcome it is supposed to drive. You are comfortable working across teams, creating structure where it does not yet exist, and building enablement that scales beyond Castlight's own sales force.

‎

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT:

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for:

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard:
Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

Requirements and benefits

Educational qualifications

  • A Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science / Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics / Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Systems or other related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree is accepted if only candidate has 5 years of experience in the field.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a minimum of 3 years of professional experience in related roles or domain - specifically for QA-automation/testing or cybersecurity roles

How it works
Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Compensation:
Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $40/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Why this freelance opportunity might be a great fit for you?

  • Take part in a part-time, remote, freelance project that fits around your primary professional or academic commitments.
  • Work on advanced AI projects and gain valuable experience that enhances your portfolio. - Influence how future AI models understand and communicate in your field of expertise.

About the team

At Zillow Group, our mission is to empower people to unlock life's next chapter. The Platform Engineering team owns the infrastructure every engineer at Zillow builds on, spanning compute and runtime, networking and connectivity, databases, secrets and identity, and the delivery tooling that moves code to production. We are shifting from an infrastructure operations model to platform-as-a-product, replacing ticket queues and manual provisioning with golden paths, self-service, and API-first interfaces so that product teams can focus on business outcomes instead of operational complexity.

Increasingly, this platform serves AI agents alongside the engineers directing them. Our self-service paths are evolving to support agent-driven, pipeline-driven, and hybrid workflows, making Platform Engineering foundational to how quickly and safely Zillow can build with AI.

About the role

As a Principal Product Manager for Platform Engineering, you will own product strategy for the platform capabilities that every engineering team at Zillow depends on. You will define the golden paths teams follow by default, drive adoption and migration onto those paths across thousands of services, and establish the measurement and value model that makes the platform's impact visible to the business.

This is the first dedicated product role in the organization. Platform Engineering has already built many of the foundations of a product operating model — customer discovery, written product requirements, and outcome metrics are how these teams work today — with engineering leaders carrying that work alongside running their teams. As a Principal Product Manager, you will raise the ceiling on that practice, partnering with engineering leadership across six teams to deepen discovery, sharpen prioritization, and organize the roadmap around customer problems and value streams rather than infrastructure layers.

Your scope spans the full platform surface — though the areas you drive most directly will be shaped by where the leverage is greatest as near-term product needs across the teams stabilize. At this level, you will define the operating model other teams plan and build within, not just execute within it yourself.

  • Own platform strategy across Platform Engineering's portfolio, turning independently run infrastructure roadmaps into a coherent product direction with explicit investment tradeoffs

  • Drive adoption and migration outcomes across teams with no reporting relationship to you, using defaults, deprecation paths, and enablement mechanisms that produce measurable change in how teams build

  • Define how applications and AI agents consume platform capabilities, establishing which self-service paths are agent-driven, which remain deterministic, and where human approval is required

  • Establish how platform success is measured — adoption, onboarding time, satisfaction, and key customer outcomes — and build the underlying value model of what capabilities cost to serve and what they are worth

  • Deepen the product operating model across six engineering teams, partnering with the engineering leaders who carry product responsibility to strengthen discovery, requirements, and outcome definition

Who you are

  • 8+ years of product management experience, including substantial time building internal platforms, infrastructure, or developer tooling used by multiple teams across organizational boundaries

  • Experience owning a platform portfolio rather than a single product area — multiple interdependent capabilities with different customers, maturity levels, and lifecycles — and prioritizing across them

  • Strong technical fluency in cloud infrastructure and distributed systems, including compute and container orchestration, networking, databases, identity and secrets, and CI/CD, sufficient to reason about architectural tradeoffs alongside senior engineers rather than gather requirements from them

  • Proven track record driving adoption of platform standards across teams you do not manage, using defaults, deprecation paths, and mechanisms that drove measurable change in behavior

  • Experience leading complex migrations at scale, including the full retirement of the systems they replaced

  • Able to operate in ambiguity and impose structure on complex, cross-functional infrastructure initiatives where scope is undefined and precedent is limited

  • Experience raising the product bar for engineering leaders who carry product responsibility, through coaching, shared standards, and durable artifacts rather than sole ownership

  • Familiarity with designing platform capabilities for AI agents as consumers, including where automated workflows require human approval and how automated paths are verified
