jobs.title: Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We’re hiring a Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs to lead how GiveWell’s work is represented in the media and in public conversations. You will set our strategy, build trusted relationships with journalists and other influential voices, pursue opportunities that increase understanding of GiveWell’s work, and lead our external response in fast-moving situations.

This role reports to Steven Profaizer, our Vice President of Communications, and will lead a small and growing team. This is one of three new communications leadership roles, alongside a Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications and a Senior Communications Officer, Editorial & Production.

About the role

Both our research and impact are expanding. Last year, we directed more than $400 million to highly cost-effective programs that save and improve lives. This year, we expect our grantmaking to approach, and possibly exceed, $1 billion.

To build toward the communications capacity this next stage requires, we are rapidly expanding our team. Together with the Vice President of Communications, the three new Senior Communications Officers will form GiveWell’s communications leadership team. Each leader will own their function, but much of the work that matters most—like team strategies, major initiatives, partnership campaigns, and how we present the organization as a whole—will involve all three. We will expect this group to set shared priorities and work closely together to achieve the team’s goals.

In this hands-on leadership position, you’ll own how and where GiveWell engages in media and public conversations, with end-to-end responsibility for this emerging function. You’ll set its strategy, hire and develop its people, build its systems, and personally own its hardest and most consequential work. This is an opportunity to build, not just inherit, an important function at a critical point in GiveWell’s development. You’ll start with a small team and grow it over time.

While this role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level, we may consider hiring an exceptional candidate as a Communications Director—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.

What You'll Do

As Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs, you will combine long-term strategy and relationship-building with the ability to respond quickly and exercise sound judgment in sensitive or fast-moving situations.

Specific duties will include:

  • Set GiveWell’s strategy across media, thought-leader engagement, online communities, public forums and events, and other earned communications opportunities—including deciding where and when GiveWell should participate and overseeing those engagements.
  • Build and maintain high-trust relationships with journalists, editors, podcast hosts, event organizers, thought leaders, subject-matter experts, and other influential external stakeholders.
  • Identify, develop, and pitch substantive stories, event opportunities, and thought-leadership ideas that extend understanding of GiveWell’s work.
  • Own inbound media engagement, including situations that require rapid responses, close coordination with subject-matter experts, and careful judgment about what GiveWell can responsibly say—and about which responses need escalation.
  • Build and maintain GiveWell’s readiness for sensitive or fast-moving situations, monitor emerging issues in media and public conversations, and lead our external response when needed in partnership with others.
  • Advise GiveWell’s leadership on external opportunities and relationships, and prepare senior leaders and subject-matter experts for interviews, speaking engagements, and other public appearances.
  • Exercise sound judgment about when and how GiveWell should enter public conversations, including evaluating likely value, reputational considerations, and communications risks.
  • Evaluate and help shape public-facing communications partnerships, advising on which opportunities GiveWell should pursue and how we should participate.
  • Serve as a spokesperson for GiveWell in select media interviews, events, and other public forums, communicating our perspective clearly, accurately, and with sound judgment.
  • Work with grantees and other partners on press releases and other media-facing communications involving GiveWell or our shared work.
  • Manage and develop one or two team members initially, and build the relationships, systems, and additional capacity the function will need over time.

About You

You are skilled at using communications to help people understand complex ideas, build trust, and take action. You are comfortable being accountable for outcomes, making consequential decisions with limited oversight, and knowing which decisions genuinely require escalation.

You are energized by intellectually demanding work, and the challenges of creating engaging communications within a careful and precise style. You can engage deeply with GiveWell’s research, and you are comfortable understanding and communicating about data in detail. You have a long track record of getting up to speed quickly on complex subject matter and carefully communicating to a very high standard. You can build a compelling narrative that is entirely factual, representing what is known and unknown without overstating or hedging into vagueness—and you find the idea of working with GiveWell’s exacting communications standards exciting rather than limiting.

Your background includes significant experience leading communications in complex, high-stakes environments. This should include 10+ years of experience in media relations, thought leadership, and public engagement. You have deep experience owning that work end to end, not just contributing to it. You’ve remained a hands-on leader who enjoys the work itself, as well as the strategy and systems behind it.

You know how journalists, influential voices, events, and other public forums shape how organizations and ideas are understood. You have a demonstrated ability to build meaningful external relationships, identify opportunities worth pursuing, personally represent an organization’s perspective, and navigate public-facing situations in which context is limited, timelines are short, and judgment matters. Much of this should be work you executed yourself, in addition to work you directed. Experience in settings where precision and credibility were at least as important as reach is a strong signal of fit.

In addition to demonstrated expertise in the duties listed above, you should have:

  • Exceptional communications judgment, including the ability to understand audience, context, risk, timing, and the underlying substance of a message.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to quickly make complex ideas clear and compelling without sacrificing rigor or nuance.
  • A track record of building and leading: you have created or substantially rebuilt a team or function—not only run ones you inherited—and you have hired, developed, and managed people.
  • Recent, hands-on excellence at your craft: you can point to work from the past few years that you personally produced or substantially shaped.
  • Experience producing communications that are direct and factual while being engaging and effective with their target audiences—work that succeeds through substance and clarity rather than embellishment.
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage deeply with GiveWell’s research and ideas, even without prior experience in our giving areas.
  • Experience advising executives or other senior decision-makers directly.
  • Strong alignment with GiveWell’s mission and values, including truth-seeking, transparency, and a commitment to communicating accurately and thoughtfully.

We also think these qualities will help you do well in the role and at GiveWell:

  • People who can develop a strong point of view and hold it with confidence, but remain genuinely open to challenge, new information, and better ideas.
  • Self-starters who take ownership, are comfortable creating structure in an evolving environment, and can make thoughtful decisions without always having complete information.
  • People who are proactive and anticipatory, who identify opportunities, risks, bottlenecks, and communications needs before they become obvious.
  • Collaborative leaders who raise the quality of the work around them and build strong relationships across teams.
  • People who coordinate well with peers, resolve dependencies and disagreements, and make shared work clearer rather than more complicated.

Key Questions & Information

What are some of the reasons I might not like this role?

  • You want to step into a mature function with established systems, rather than build one while you run it.
  • You do best with clear direction and established priorities. We’ll expect you to set most of your own, make most decisions yourself, and reach substantial autonomy within your first six months.
  • You prefer advising on communications to producing and being accountable for them.
  • You want sole ownership of an organization’s overarching communications strategy and brand. At GiveWell, the Vice President of Communications owns that direction; you would help shape it and lead your function within it.
  • You want to lead a large team from day one. This team is small today, and much of the most difficult work will be yours to do directly.
  • You find standards of precision and understatement limiting and frustrating. We work extremely hard to only communicate accurately what we know and what we don’t.

Can I apply to more than one of the Senior Communications Officer roles?

You can, but most people shouldn’t. We’re looking for deep expertise in these areas, and we expect most candidates with required expertise will be a clear fit for a single role. If you’re one of the few with real depth in more than one area, apply to both and tell us why. Otherwise, apply for the role you are most qualified for, and we’ll let you know if we think another role might suit you better.

What does this interview process entail?

We’ll use a combination of interviews, written exercises, and work trials to assess the qualities described above. We’ll share more specific details if we invite you to move forward to any of the following stages, but our current plan is:

  • Application
  • Interview with a member of the Talent Acquisition Team
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial
  • Interview with the Vice President of Communications
  • Values interview
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial with the Vice President of Communications
  • CEO interview and References

Note that you don’t need to submit a cover letter. We rely heavily on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we’re making early decisions. We encourage you to spend time responding to the application questions thoroughly and carefully.

Details

  • Team: You’ll report to our Vice President of Communications, collaborate closely with the two other Senior Communications Officers, and lead a small team that you’ll develop over time.
  • Compensation: This role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level. For an exceptional candidate, we may consider hiring at the Communications Director level—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $250,000
    • All other U.S. locations: $225,000
    • International: Custom based on location. We can give you a specific number at the penultimate stage of the hiring process.
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California, or Brooklyn, NYC.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. Given the managerial nature of this role, a successful candidate will need to work hours that have a certain minimum overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Travel: Communications staff members should expect to attend three week-long retreats each year to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. Other domestic and international travel may be required, but isn’t expected to be a regular part of these roles. We’ll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll give reasonable consideration to staff who have family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. Beyond the requirements of those laws, we value our team’s diversity in all respects, and we desire to maintain a work environment free of harassment or discrimination—we want our team members to thrive at GiveWell. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at . We will consider employment for qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that you have read and consent to GiveWell's Privacy Statement for Applicants. By completing an application exercise, you acknowledge and assent to GiveWell's Work Trial Policy.

jobs.title: Competitive Programming Expert - Freelance AI Trainer
jobs.excerpt: Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.
jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves

We're building competitive-programming problems and their automatic graders (test cases + checkers) used to train advanced AI coding models. You'll create problems, write both correct and deliberately-wrong solutions, and design the tough test cases that catch subtly-broken code. Your work is what makes the training signal trustworthy.

To apply, share: your competitive-programming handle(s) + current/peak rating, any problem-setting experience, and IOI/ICPC/olympiad history.

What you'll do

  • Write original algorithmic problems — clear statement, sound constraints, an intended solution;
  • Write correct solutions in C++ and Python;
  • Write realistic wrong solutions (common mistakes) to test against;
  • Build and harden test cases: generators, edge cases, stress and "hacking" tests;
  • Write checkers/interactors (testlib) for problems with more than one valid answer;
  • Confirm the quality bar: correct solutions pass, wrong ones fail, within time limits.

What we look for

  • Strong competitive programming background, shown by a public profile — a Codeforces rating (see levels below), OR an IOI / ICPC / national-olympiad record;
  • Fluent contest C++ (STL, complexity); comfortable writing Python;
  • Can explain why a solution is wrong and build an input that breaks it;
  • Strong written English (C1+).

Levels (by Codeforces rating, or equivalent olympiad achievement):

  • Associate — 1700–2100 (Expert / Candidate Master): easier problems;
  • Expert — 2200–2600 (Master / Grandmaster): harder problems
  • Senior / Reviewer — 2600+ (Int'l Grandmaster) or IOI/ICPC medalist: hardest problems + quality review.

Nice to have

  • IOI / ICPC alumni and top competitive programmers especially encouraged to apply;
  • Experience setting or testing problems for real contests (Codeforces rounds, ICPC, national olympiads, online judges);
  • Testlib experience (checkers, validators, generators);
  • Experience creating data for LLM code benchmarks or similar RL / evaluation datasets.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $90/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #


26WD100797

Account Based Marketing Manager – Nordics

We are looking for an experienced Account Based Marketing Manager – Nordics to help deepen Autodesk’s relationships with strategic customers and accelerate growth across the region, with particular focus on Sweden, Norway, and Denmark.

The Opportunity:

As the Account Based Marketing Manager for the Nordics, you will develop and lead targeted marketing strategies for a defined portfolio of high-value accounts and account groups. Working closely with Sales and teams across Marketing, Customer Success, Operations, and the partner ecosystem, you will identify where account-based marketing can make the greatest commercial impact and translate customer intelligence into coordinated, relevant engagement.

This role goes beyond executing campaigns. You will connect account strategy, buying-group insight, customer needs, sales action, and marketing activation to create measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes. You will design personalised 1:1 and 1:Few ABM programmes, activate decision-makers and influencers across the customer journey, and use data and intent signals to determine the next best action.

The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking with practical execution. You will be comfortable moving between account planning, stakeholder collaboration, campaign development, performance analysis, and continuous optimisation in a fast-changing global organisation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partner with Nordic Sales leadership and account teams to identify and prioritise strategic accounts based on revenue potential, business priorities, customer fit, intent signals, and opportunity data.
  • Co-create integrated account and account-group plans, including objectives, buying-group strategies, engagement journeys, messaging, campaign calendars, ownership, and next-best actions.
  • Research priority accounts to understand their business drivers, transformation priorities, competitive environments, decision processes, and stakeholder relationships.
  • Map buying groups, including decision-makers, influencers, practitioners, and executive stakeholders, and develop strategies to improve engagement and relationship coverage.
  • Design and deliver personalised 1:1 and 1:few account-based marketing programmes across digital, content, events, executive engagement, sales outreach, SDR, customer, and partner channels.
  • Adapt global go-to-market priorities, industry narratives, customer stories, and value propositions for Nordic audiences, account segments, personas, and opportunity stages.
  • Use intent, engagement, product, opportunity, install-base, and relationship signals to trigger relevant plays and guide marketing and sales activity.
  • Equip Sales teams with account intelligence, tailored messaging, campaign assets, conversation starters, and practical recommendations for account progression.
  • Coordinate with Field Marketing to integrate regional events, executive programmes, and customer engagement moments into strategic account plans.
  • Collaborate with Marketing Operations and Analytics on account segmentation, scoring, routing, dashboards, attribution, and performance reporting.
  • Work with channel and alliance partners on co-marketing, co-sell engagement, ecosystem influence, and account penetration.
  • Manage programmes and priorities independently while maintaining strong alignment across Nordic, EMEA, and global stakeholders.
  • Measure and communicate performance against shared objectives, including account engagement, buying-group coverage, pipeline creation and influence, opportunity acceleration, conversion, expansion, and account-level revenue contribution.
  • Run regular performance reviews with Sales and Marketing stakeholders, identify obstacles, capture insights, and continuously optimise account strategies and programmes.

Key Competencies

  • Account-Based Marketing Expertise: Strong understanding of account selection, tiering, buying-group engagement, account planning, and 1:1 and 1 marketing motions.
  • Commercial and Customer Focus: Ability to connect customer needs, marketing activity, sales priorities, pipeline progression, and revenue outcomes.
  • Account Intelligence and Data Fluency: Skilled at turning account research, intent, engagement, product, opportunity, and relationship signals into actionable strategies.
  • Sales Partnership and Influence: Ability to build trusted relationships with Sales and other stakeholders, align around shared goals, and influence effectively without direct authority.
  • Integrated Campaign Orchestration: Experience coordinating personalised journeys across digital, content, events, executive engagement, SDR, customer, and partner channels.
  • Measurement and Optimisation: Strong analytical approach to evaluating account engagement, buying-group coverage, pipeline impact, conversion, and revenue contribution.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work across Sales, Field Marketing, Customer Success, Marketing Operations, Content, Product Marketing, and partner teams.
  • Communication, Agility, and Ownership: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and adapt quickly in a matrixed environment.

Minimum Qualifications

  • BA, B.Comm, or equivalent degree in Marketing, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent relevant work experience.
  • Eight or more years of experience in B2B marketing, key-account marketing, account-based marketing, demand generation, or a closely related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing marketing programmes for strategic or enterprise accounts.
  • Understanding of regional go-to-market dynamics across the Nordics, particularly Sweden, Norway, and Denmark.
  • Fluency in Swedish and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and influence stakeholders in a fast-changing, matrixed environment.
  • A self-starting approach, with the ability to work independently, take initiative, manage multiple priorities, and move projects forward proactively.
  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills and experience working closely with Sales or account-management teams.
  • Experience developing campaign materials, including creative and content briefs, messaging, presentations, sales-enablement materials, and customer-facing assets.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to assess and report on marketing and sales performance.
  • Experience using marketing and account-intelligence platforms such as 6sense, Allocadia, and Marketo.
  • Practical experience using large language model tools such as ChatGPT or Claude to support research, planning, content development, or marketing productivity.
  • Familiarity with marketing analytics, reporting, attribution, or business-intelligence tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience marketing to architecture, engineering, construction, manufacturing, or adjacent technology audiences.
  • Experience marketing to public-sector organisations is advantageous but not required.
  • Experience working in a global organisation with regional and centralised teams.
  • Confidence operating in a matrixed environment where influence, judgement, and effective prioritisation are essential.
  • Experience working with complex buying groups, long sales cycles, and enterprise-level customer relationships.
  • Familiarity with customer expansion, retention, adoption, or lifecycle marketing strategies.
  • Experience coordinating programmes with partners, alliances, or channel organisations.
  • A practical and commercially minded approach, balanced with creativity, curiosity, and a willingness to test new ideas.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will be demonstrated through stronger engagement and preference within priority Nordic accounts, broader coverage of relevant buying groups, close alignment between Sales and Marketing, and measurable contribution to pipeline creation, opportunity acceleration, customer expansion, and account-level revenue.

You will help Autodesk focus its go-to-market resources on the accounts that matter most, create customer engagement that is genuinely relevant, and establish account-based marketing as a coordinated revenue motion rather than a collection of disconnected campaigns.

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.


We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

jobs.excerpt: Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.
jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves

We're building competitive-programming problems and their automatic graders (test cases + checkers) used to train advanced AI coding models. You'll create problems, write both correct and deliberately-wrong solutions, and design the tough test cases that catch subtly-broken code. Your work is what makes the training signal trustworthy.

To apply, share: your competitive-programming handle(s) + current/peak rating, any problem-setting experience, and IOI/ICPC/olympiad history.

What you'll do

  • Write original algorithmic problems — clear statement, sound constraints, an intended solution;
  • Write correct solutions in C++ and Python;
  • Write realistic wrong solutions (common mistakes) to test against;
  • Build and harden test cases: generators, edge cases, stress and "hacking" tests;
  • Write checkers/interactors (testlib) for problems with more than one valid answer;
  • Confirm the quality bar: correct solutions pass, wrong ones fail, within time limits.

What we look for

  • Strong competitive programming background, shown by a public profile — a Codeforces rating (see levels below), OR an IOI / ICPC / national-olympiad record;
  • Fluent contest C++ (STL, complexity); comfortable writing Python;
  • Can explain why a solution is wrong and build an input that breaks it;
  • Strong written English (C1+).

Levels (by Codeforces rating, or equivalent olympiad achievement):

  • Associate — 1700–2100 (Expert / Candidate Master): easier problems;
  • Expert — 2200–2600 (Master / Grandmaster): harder problems
  • Senior / Reviewer — 2600+ (Int'l Grandmaster) or IOI/ICPC medalist: hardest problems + quality review.

Nice to have

  • IOI / ICPC alumni and top competitive programmers especially encouraged to apply;
  • Experience setting or testing problems for real contests (Codeforces rounds, ICPC, national olympiads, online judges);
  • Testlib experience (checkers, validators, generators);
  • Experience creating data for LLM code benchmarks or similar RL / evaluation datasets.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $90/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.excerpt: The climate crisis is the defining challenge of our time—but it’s also the greatest opportunity for innovation, and a challenge we’re proud to take on.
jobs.description:
The climate crisis is the defining challenge of our time—but it’s also the greatest opportunity for innovation, and a challenge we’re proud to take on. At Overstory, we’re harnessing cutting-edge technology to enable a resilient electrical grid that keeps communities thriving as our world changes.

The grid is the backbone of life as we know it. It powers hospitals, keeps food fresh, and ensures communities stay connected. But extreme weather, aging infrastructure, and growing wildfire risks are putting this critical system under pressure. All of this combined makes the electric utility industry the greatest opportunity for tackling climate change.

One of the leading causes of catastrophic wildfires and power outages? Trees and brush coming into contact with power lines.

That’s where we help. At Overstory, we use AI and advanced satellite imagery to pinpoint and prioritize vegetation risks before they materialize. By giving utilities critical analysis on those risks, we’re helping prevent outages, reduce wildfire risks, and accelerate the transition to a safer, more resilient grid.

Our team spans the Americas and Europe, and we work with utility partners across the Americas and beyond. We’re outdoor enthusiasts, musicians, artists, athletes, parents, and adventurers. What unites us is a passion for solving complex problems, a commitment to climate action, and the belief that technology should be a force for good.

Join us to help us build a more resilient world together.

The Role

As the CTO of Overstory, you will lead and scale a world-class engineering team that reduces the risk of wildfires and power outages around the world. This is a rare opportunity for a seasoned engineering leader to help guide a commercially successful climate-tech company through its next stage of growth.

Following our Series B, we’re entering a phase of rapid expansion. You will define a compelling technical strategy and build the team to deliver it. This role requires someone who can zoom in and out seamlessly — rolling up your sleeves to solve complex technical problems while also communicating effectively with the board.

Our product sits at the intersection of AI and remote sensing — fields evolving at light speed. The work is exciting, mission-driven, and core to transforming the electric utility industry and creating a more resilient grid. But it comes with ambiguity. We’re looking for someone energized by the unknown, eager to build products customers love through bold, creative approaches. You must be comfortable balancing the needs of a growing business with building scalable solutions for the future — and be ready to move with urgency on both.

Time zone requirement: Europe (GMT/WET, CET) and Eastern United States (EST)

What A Successful Candidate Looks Like

You’re an entrepreneurial startup leader with a track record of leading engineering teams from Series A through Series C and beyond with a mix of boldness and empathy. You understand the ups and downs that are normal at VC-backed startups. You know how to inspire global teams with an exciting vision while offering them the hands-on support to bring it to life.

You have a strong network to tap, and you are bold in your recruiting. You’re not afraid to hire people who know more than you and to stretch for top talent, and you understand that recruiting is a top priority that requires constant networking and attention. You will build a diverse team that has a high-performing, inclusive, and caring culture.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the development of all of Overstory’s technology, including our software product, our ML models, the internal tools we use and the platform that underlies it all.
  • Work in close partnership with our VP Product & Strategy to propel the business forward with the product we are developing. You’ll work to deeply understand our customers' problems so that you can lead bold engineering initiatives to solve them.
  • Build a high-performing and diverse engineering team that works remotely from multiple countries, and across multiple time zones.
  • Create a compelling technical vision and translate that into a strategy for the next 12-36 months.
  • Lead highly productive cross-functional teams that ship a high-quality product on a daily basis.
  • Foster an inclusive culture where everyone can do their best work.
  • Create strong lines of communication within your team and partnerships with other key parts of the business.

About You

Traits we value:

  • Boldness: You’re not afraid to make hard decisions and take risks, and you always act with urgency.
  • Mission-driven: You care deeply about building great products that help communities adapt to climate change by creating a more resilient electrical grid.
  • Empathy: You can attract and develop a diverse team, and you are inclusive in your approach to leadership.
  • Listening: You lead with inquiry. You make people on your own team and across the company feel heard.
  • Curiosity: Learning excites you, and you’re not afraid to admit what you don’t know.
  • Clarity: You’re a simplifier, not a complicator, and you can communicate clearly to a broad audience without using jargon.
  • Collaborative spirit: Team above ego, and you’re never afraid to get your hands dirty.

Experience we value:

  • You have managed a team of 70+ people.
  • You have been on a VC-backed startup journey from Series A through Series C or later, and you know how to scale a team successfully through those transitions. You value the entrepreneurial “get it done fast” spirit of the early days, while also setting a standard for excellence that will scale to later stages.
  • You have experience working on a complex, ML-based product. Bonus points for geospatial or remote sensing experience.
  • You have a deep understanding of software development processes and are product-centric in the way you think about building technology.
  • You have experienced the value of cross-functional teams where engineering, product and design work side-by-side.
  • You have managed remote teams.
  • You have managed global teams.

What We Offer

  • Competitive, location-specific compensation and benefits
  • Flexible, autonomous and collaborative working environment rooted in trust - we build our work days around our lives, not the other way around
  • Home office stipend, coworking and ongoing education budgets
  • A company culture that genuinely embodies each of our core values
  • To be part of truly mission-driven work that reduces wildfires, protects earth’s natural resources and helps solve our climate crisis

About Our Team

We are a fast-growing team of about 100 people from all over the world. Fifteen nationalities are represented and at last count we speak fourteen languages: English, Dutch, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Luxembourgish, Lithuanian, Bulgarian, Finnish, Estonian, and Afrikaans.

We work remotely from eleven countries and are looking for candidates that are living and working in one of them: United States, the Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Estonia, Portugal, France, Sweden, Switzerland, Denmark and Canada. We gather once a year in-person for our unforgettable team gathering event. We also offer the option to occasionally meet up for in-person collaboration.

Diversity & Inclusion

The climate crisis is a human crisis that requires diverse perspectives to solve.

We place enormous value on diversity and believe that the best ideas emerge when people with different backgrounds and experience work together. We remain committed to scaling a team that reflects the communities we serve, and strive to uphold equitable and inclusive practices across every aspect of our business. We are responsible for creating and maintaining a culture where everyone - regardless of background - has a voice in building a sustainable future.

Our Values

Tackling the climate crisis is our greatest mission.

We act with urgency.

Our curiosity fuels our growth.

We recognize that change is constant, and we find joy and power in exploration.

We’re rooted in diversity.

Just as ecosystems need biodiversity to thrive, our resiliency comes from our differences.

We care for each other.

We love the power of machines but we nurture each other as humans.

Trust is fundamental.

We assume the best in everyone, and we share ideas openly so that we have a positive impact.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We sometimes use AI tools to support parts of our hiring process, such as helping us manage applications more efficiently or ensuring job descriptions are clear and inclusive. All hiring decisions are always made by people, not machines. Any data processed by AI is handled securely in line with GDPR and our Privacy Notice.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Senior Database Administrator (DBA) focused on the operational reliability of database platforms across AWS Commercial and AWS GovCloud environments. This is a hands-on role that combines software engineering practices with database operations to ensure data platforms are reliable, scalable, secure, and highly available.

The Senior DBA will define and monitor SLIs and SLOs for database services and own their reliability, availability, performance, capacity planning, recoverability, and operational lifecycle. The role will lead incident response, perform root-cause analysis, and drive automation that reduces manual work and eliminates operational toil. This person will also partner closely with platform engineering, security, and application development teams to ensure database services meet application requirements and security standards and are delivered in a consistent, reliable, and supportable manner.

Work Location: Remote

Shift Schedule: 8am – 5pm Eastern Standard Time (EST)

What you will do:

  • Operate production databases on AWS, including RDS and Aurora (PostgreSQL and MySQL), as well as self-managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server on VMs as needed.
  • Administer DynamoDB, ElastiCache (Redis), and OpenSearch supporting application workloads and caching.
  • Own database architecture, performance tuning, capacity planning, and right-sizing.
  • Manage backup, restore, snapshot, and point-in-time recovery strategies, and validate RTO/RPO through scheduled restore and failover testing.
  • Design, test, and maintain high-availability and disaster recovery solutions, including Multi-AZ, cross-region replication, and documented failover procedures.
  • Define and maintain SLIs/SLOs for database availability, latency, replication lag, and query performance.

  • Manage the database lifecycle, including upgrades, patching, configuration changes, maintenance, and technology refreshes.
  • Improve database resilience through capacity planning, performance testing, failure-mode analysis, disaster recovery, and recovery testing.
  • Identify and address reliability risks and technical debt using reliability metrics, incident trends, capacity data, and service health indicators.
  • Automate database operations using an everything-as-code approach to improve consistency, repeatability, testing, recovery, and efficiency.
  • Partner with Platform Engineering and application teams to define operational requirements, improve reusable infrastructure, and strengthen database reliability and operability.

Technologies and Skillsets:

  • AWS data services (RDS, Aurora for PostgreSQL and MySQL, DynamoDB, ElastiCache) and core services (EC2, VPC, IAM, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch)
  • Relational database administration: PostgreSQL and MySQL, with Oracle or SQL Server experience valued
  • Advanced SQL, query optimization, execution plan analysis, and index and schema design
  • High availability, replication, backup and recovery, and disaster recovery design and testing
  • Dynatrace, Datadog, and OpenTelemetry for database and application observability
  • Terraform and Ansible / Ansible Tower for infrastructure and configuration automation
  • GitLab, Jenkins, and database schema migration tooling such as Liquibase or Flyway
  • Sonatype Nexus and Aqua Security
  • Python, Bash, or Go
  • RHEL Linux administration
  • Windows Server

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

  • Must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain the required Public Trust level clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree and 8 years of experience, a Master's degree with 6 years of experience, or a High School Diploma or equivalent and 12 years of experience.
  • 5+ years of database administration, data platform engineering, or SRE experience with significant production database ownership.
  • Hands-on production experience operating database services on AWS at scale.
  • DoD 8570/8140 compliant certification.
  • Demonstrated experience with backup, recovery, and disaster recovery execution, including validated restore testing.
  • Demonstrated experience defining and implementing SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets for data services.
  • Proven incident management experience, including on-call ownership and root-cause analysis.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and strong communication, with the ability to present performance and reliability insights to technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • AWS Certified Database Specialty, Solutions Architect, or SysOps Administrator.
  • PostgreSQL or MySQL professional certification.
  • HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate.
  • Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or experience running stateful workloads on Kubernetes or OpenShift (ROSA).
  • Dynatrace or Datadog vendor certification.
  • Experience with database automation at scale, including fleet-wide patching and self-service provisioning.
  • Experience operating multi-tenant data platforms with tenant isolation and noisy-neighbor mitigation.
  • Experience supporting FedRAMP, FISMA, or DoD-accredited environments.

Job Title: Senior Director, Quality & Regulatory Notified Body Audits

Job Description Summary

The Senior Director, Q&R Notified Body Audits provides global leadership for Notified Body engagement, certification strategy, audit governance, and regulatory compliance activities across GE HealthCare. Serving as the primary interface between GE HealthCare, Notified Bodies, certification bodies, and manufacturing and development sites worldwide, this role drives audit readiness, oversees certification activities, manages regulatory risk, and aligns regulatory expectations across jurisdictions. The position establishes and continuously improves global processes supporting Notified Body interactions, audits, technical reviews, certifications, and regulatory compliance.

The Senior Director also leads QMS integration assessments associated with acquisitions, mergers, divestitures, and business expansions, including evaluation of quality system maturity, compliance, certification impacts, and integration risks. The role provides executive-level recommendations, develops governance models and reporting metrics, and serves as a strategic advisor to Quality, Regulatory, and business leadership. As a recognized subject matter expert, the Senior Director drives process excellence, continuous improvement, and organizational readiness to support sustained compliance and business objectives.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Represents GE HealthCare to Notified Bodies, certification bodies, auditing organizations, and external regulatory stakeholders, establishing strategic relationships that support certification activities, regulatory compliance, and business objectives.

  • Owns the enterprise strategy for Notified Body engagement and certification management, including certification transfers, scope expansions, site additions, legal entity changes, remediation strategies, and certification pathway planning.

  • Provides strategic oversight and governance of Notified Body audits, technical documentation assessments, surveillance audits, recertification audits, and unannounced audits, including risk assessment, escalation management, and issue resolution. Develops, standardizes, and continuously improves tools and standard work supporting Notified Body engagement.

  • Serves as the primary point of contact between GE HealthCare and Notified Bodies, driving contract negotiations and resolving certification, compliance, capacity, and service-related concerns.

  • Leads QMS post-acquisition integration assessments for acquisitions, mergers, divestitures, and business expansions, including compliance evaluations, certification impact assessments, and supporting integration planning.

  • Generates metrics, trend analyses, executive dashboards, and leadership presentations related to audit performance, certification status, compliance risks, Notified Body effectiveness, and QMS integration activities.

  • Leads through complexity by managing competing priorities across regions, business units, product lines, and regulatory frameworks while building consensus among internal and external stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree and a minimum of 10 years’ experience in the medical device industry; or bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 15 years’ experience in the medical device industry.

  • Demonstrated understanding of Medical Device QMS and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820, EU MDR, MDSAP and ISO 13485.

  • Minimum 5 years of progressive Quality and/or Regulatory Affairs experience at a GE HealthCare site, with demonstrated responsibility for supporting or leading interactions with Notified Bodies during audits, certifications, surveillance activities, technical reviews, or compliance-related engagements.

  • Demonstrated experience developing metrics, analyzing quality or regulatory data, identifying trends, and preparing executive-level communications or presentations to support decision-making.

  • Demonstrated expertise communicating across all levels of the organization on design controls, design verification and validation, production and process controls, CAPA, complaints, risk management, certification strategy, and regulatory compliance expectations.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with a demonstrated commitment to integrity, ethical decision-making, and professional conduct.

Desired Characteristics

  • Demonstrated understanding of medical device and quality management system certification programs, including EU MDR, MDSAP, ISO 13485, ISO 9001, UKCA, legal entity considerations, and certification management strategies.

  • Experience working directly with Notified Bodies, certification bodies, auditing organizations, regulators, or external regulatory stakeholders in a global medical device environment including managing certification portfolios, Notified Body relationships, contract negotiations, service expectations, and associated budgets.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence organizational strategy and drive alignment across global functions, business units, sites, executive leaders, and external stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, interpret technical documentation, convert data into actionable insights, and communicate risks clearly.

  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 20%.

jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We’re hiring a Senior Communications Officer, Editorial & Production to lead the editorial quality and production of GiveWell’s communications. You will set the editorial bar, build the people and systems needed to produce excellent work consistently and at increasing scale, and personally shape some of our most complex and consequential content.

This role reports to Steven Profaizer, our Vice President of Communications, and will lead a small and growing team. This is one of three new communications leadership roles, alongside a Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications and a Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs.

About the role

Both our research and impact are expanding. Last year, we directed more than $400 million to highly cost-effective programs that save and improve lives. This year, we expect our grantmaking to approach, and possibly exceed, $1 billion.

To build toward the communications capacity this next stage requires, we are rapidly expanding our team. Together with the Vice President of Communications, the three new Senior Communications Officers will form GiveWell’s communications leadership team. Each leader will own their function, but much of the work that matters most—like team strategies, major initiatives, partnership campaigns, and how we present the organization as a whole—will involve all three. We will expect this group to set shared priorities and work closely together to achieve the team’s goals.

In this hands-on leadership position, you’ll own the editorial quality and production of GiveWell’s communications, with end-to-end responsibility for this emerging function. You’ll strengthen its standards, hire and develop its people, build its systems, and personally own its hardest and most consequential work. This is an opportunity to build, not just inherit, an important function at a critical point in GiveWell’s development. You’ll start with a small team and grow it over time.

While this role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level, we may consider hiring an exceptional candidate as a Communications Director—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.

What You'll Do

As Senior Communications Officer, Editorial & Production, you will be responsible not only for the quality of individual pieces but also for creating a content operation that can prioritize effectively, manage dependencies, use its resources well, and deliver reliably. This will require both senior editorial judgment and strong operational leadership.

Specific duties will include:

  • Own the editorial quality and production of GiveWell’s communications, ensuring that our work is clear, accurate, useful, carefully reasoned, and delivered on time. You will serve as GiveWell’s senior editor for our communications content, with responsibility for returning or correcting work that does not meet our editorial bar.
  • Build and manage the workflows, editorial standards, review processes, and production systems that allow GiveWell to create consistently excellent content at increasing scale.
  • Lead planning, prioritization, and resource allocation for GiveWell’s owned-content portfolio, managing dependencies and moving complex projects from concept through publication.
  • Uphold GiveWell’s voice and editorial standards across everything we publish, and help colleagues across the organization write within them.
  • Own the development of GiveWell’s recurring communications and reporting products, turning established priorities and messaging into clear, accurate content.
  • Personally create, edit, or substantially shape our most complex, sensitive, or high-priority content.
  • Oversee GiveWell’s website content operations, including the people and processes responsible for routine updates and publishing, so that the site remains accurate, current, and consistent with our editorial standards.
  • Serve as a senior editorial and production partner to teams across GiveWell, helping shape high-priority projects early, determine the right format and production approach, and establish clear roles, review paths, and timelines.
  • Oversee the production of design, visual, and multimedia assets across GiveWell’s channels, and the internal team and external contractors who create them.
  • Manage and develop one or two team members initially, and determine how the function’s team and capabilities should grow over time.

About You

You are skilled at using communications to help people understand complex ideas, build trust, and take action. You are comfortable being accountable for outcomes, making consequential decisions with limited oversight, and knowing which decisions genuinely require escalation.

You are energized by intellectually demanding work, and the challenges of creating engaging communications within a careful and precise style. You can engage deeply with GiveWell’s research, and you are comfortable understanding and communicating about data in detail. You have a long track record of getting up to speed quickly on complex subject matter and carefully communicating to a very high standard. You can build a compelling narrative that is entirely factual, representing what is known and unknown without overstating or hedging into vagueness—and you find the idea of working with GiveWell’s exacting communications standards exciting rather than limiting.

Your background includes significant experience leading communications in complex, high-stakes environments. This should include 10+ years of experience leading editorial and content-production work, setting and maintaining editorial standards, managing writers and editors, and building systems that produce consistently high-quality work. You have deep experience owning that work end to end, not just contributing to it. You’ve remained a hands-on leader who enjoys the work itself, as well as the strategy and systems behind it.

You are a precise editor of complex or technical content: you read text literally and carefully, and you notice when a claim isn’t supported by the evidence behind it. You should be able to combine high standards for individual work with the operational judgment needed to prioritize, allocate resources, manage complex production, and increase capacity over time. You should understand how content is developed through writing, editing, design, audio, graphics, websites, and other formats—even if you are not personally an expert in every medium.

In addition to demonstrated expertise in the duties listed above, you should have:

  • Exceptional communications judgment, including the ability to understand audience, context, risk, timing, and the underlying substance of a message.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to quickly make complex ideas clear and compelling without sacrificing rigor or nuance.
  • A track record of building and leading: you have created or substantially rebuilt a team or function—not only run ones you inherited—and you have hired, developed, and managed people.
  • Recent, hands-on excellence at your craft: you can point to work from the past few years that you personally produced or substantially shaped.
  • Experience producing communications that are direct and factual while being engaging and effective with their target audiences—work that succeeds through substance and clarity rather than embellishment.
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage deeply with GiveWell’s research and ideas, even without prior experience in our giving areas.
  • Experience advising executives or other senior decision-makers directly.
  • Strong alignment with GiveWell’s mission and values, including truth-seeking, transparency, and a commitment to communicating accurately and thoughtfully.

We also think these qualities will help you do well in the role and at GiveWell:

  • People who can develop a strong point of view and hold it with confidence, but remain genuinely open to challenge, new information, and better ideas.
  • Self-starters who take ownership, are comfortable creating structure in an evolving environment, and can make thoughtful decisions without always having complete information.
  • People who are proactive and anticipatory, who identify opportunities, risks, bottlenecks, and communications needs before they become obvious.
  • Collaborative leaders who raise the quality of the work around them and build strong relationships across teams.
  • People who coordinate well with peers, resolve dependencies and disagreements, and make shared work clearer rather than more complicated.

Key Questions & Information

What are some of the reasons I might not like this role?

  • You want to step into a mature function with established systems, rather than build one while you run it.
  • You do best with clear direction and established priorities. We’ll expect you to set most of your own, make most decisions yourself, and reach substantial autonomy within your first six months.
  • You prefer advising on communications to producing and being accountable for them.
  • You want sole ownership of an organization’s overarching communications strategy and brand. At GiveWell, the Vice President of Communications owns that direction; you would help shape it and lead your function within it.
  • You want to lead a large team from day one. This team is small today, and much of the most difficult work will be yours to do directly.
  • You find standards of precision and understatement limiting and frustrating. We work extremely hard to only communicate accurately what we know and what we don’t.

Can I apply to more than one of the Senior Communications Officer roles?

You can, but most people shouldn’t. We’re looking for deep expertise in these areas, and we expect most candidates with required expertise will be a clear fit for a single role. If you’re one of the few with real depth in more than one area, apply to both and tell us why. Otherwise, apply for the role you are most qualified for, and we’ll let you know if we think another role might suit you better.

What does this interview process entail?

We’ll use a combination of interviews, written exercises, and work trials to assess the qualities described above. We’ll share more specific details if we invite you to move forward to any of the following stages, but our current plan is:

  • Application
  • Interview with a member of the Talent Acquisition Team
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial
  • Interview with the Vice President of Communications
  • Values interview
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial with the Vice President of Communications
  • CEO interview and References

Note that you don’t need to submit a cover letter. We rely heavily on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we’re making early decisions. We encourage you to spend time responding to the application questions thoroughly and carefully.

Details

  • Team: You’ll report to our Vice President of Communications, collaborate closely with the two other Senior Communications Officers, and lead a small team that you’ll develop over time.
  • Compensation: This role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level. For an exceptional candidate, we may consider hiring at the Communications Director level—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $250,000
    • All other U.S. locations: $225,000
    • International: Custom based on location. We can give you a specific number at the penultimate stage of the hiring process.
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California, or Brooklyn, NYC.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. Given the managerial nature of this role, a successful candidate will need to work hours that have a certain minimum overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Travel: Communications staff members should expect to attend three week-long retreats each year to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. Other domestic and international travel may be required, but isn’t expected to be a regular part of these roles. We’ll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll give reasonable consideration to staff who have family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

GiveWell is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer by choice. At minimum, this means that we comply with all federal, state, and local EEO and employment laws. Beyond the requirements of those laws, we value our team’s diversity in all respects, and we desire to maintain a work environment free of harassment or discrimination—we want our team members to thrive at GiveWell. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at . We will consider employment for qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that you have read and consent to GiveWell's Privacy Statement for Applicants. By completing an application exercise, you acknowledge and assent to GiveWell's Work Trial Policy.

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT:

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for:

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard:
Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

Requirements and benefits

Educational qualifications

  • A Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science / Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics / Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Systems or other related fields.

Job Family

About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

   

Who We Are

 

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life.

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

What We Do

Transamerica is organized into three distinct businesses. These include 1) World Financial Group, including Transamerica Financial Advisors, 2) Protection Solutions and Savings & Investments, comprised of life insurance, annuities, employee benefits, retirement plans, and Transamerica Investment Solutions, and 3) Financial Assets, which includes legacy blocks of long term care, universal life, and variable and fixed annuities. These are supported by Transamerica Corporate, which includes Finance, People and Places, General Counsel, Risk, Internal Audit, Strategy and Development, and Corporate Affairs, which covers Communications, Brand, and Government and Policy Affairs.

Transamerica employs nearly 7,000 people. It’s part of Aegon, an integrated, diversified, international financial services group servingapproximately 23.9 million customersworldwide.* For more information, visit transamerica.com. 

Job Description Summary

Design, develop, deploy, and support artificial intelligence (AI) solutions that improve products, services, and business processes across the organization. Leverage advanced AI engineering, cloud-native development, and software engineering practices to deliver scalable, secure, and responsible AI applications and platforms.

Responsibilities

• Collaborate with business, architecture, security, and platform teams to deliver AI solutions and communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.

Qualifications

• Professional certifications in cloud-native technologies

Working Conditions

Compensation

The Salary for this position generally ranges between 131,000-165,000 annually. Please note that the salary range is a good faith estimate for this position and actual starting pay is determined by several factors including qualifications, experience, geography, work location designation (in-office, hybrid, remote) and operational needs. Salary may vary above and below the stated amounts, as permitted by applicable law.

Enterprise Technology is a global Aegon/Transamerica organization that enables the business to move quickly and deliver the best possible outcomes for clients, while keeping their information safe and secure.

With more than 1,000 employees across the UK, US, Netherlands, Hungary, Spain, and Hong Kong, Enterprise Technology is a diverse, global team. Our experts work across areas such as application development, information security, infrastructure, data & analytics, risk & controls, program management, and architecture. Curiosity is the quality we value most. Much of our work involves solving complex problems, applying knowledge in new ways, and continuously improving how we operate. Inclusion & Diversity 

 

We believe our commitment to diversity and inclusion creates a work environment filled with exceptional individuals. Giving Back

Through a mix of financial grants and the volunteer efforts of our employees, the foundation supports nonprofit organizations focused on the things that matter most to our people in the communities where we live and work.
